newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's Blair says govt secretly rules out EMU.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's Blair says govt secretly rules out EMU.

text.p: Opposition Labour Party leader Tony Blair said on Friday that Britain's Conservative government has secretly ruled out joining a single European currency and challenged it to come clean.

"They say to certain of the media...we (the government) have ruled out a single currency. It's not on. No way. We'll never do it. Not now. Not ever," Blair said in a speech prepared for deliver to the 'What The Papers Say' awards ceremony in London.
"But they are engaged in telling the rest of us and Europe that the options are open. Either they are or they aren't."

The Conservative government's fault line on Europe gaped wide open again on Wednesday when Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said that on balance the government was "hostile" to European economic and monetary union (EMU).
Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke -- widely seen as the most pro-European member of the government -- dismissed the comments as a "slip of the tongue".
